description.narrative: In the Diffa region, the humanitarian situation remains very critical in 2026. It is characterized by massive population displacements, severe food insecurity, and significant access constraints for humanitarian actors. The region is home to more than 270,000 people who have been forcibly displaced (refugees, internally displaced persons, asylum seekers, and returnees). In terms of food security, the region is classified as being in a crisis phase (IPC Phase 3), and the populations—both host communities and displaced people—are largely dependent on humanitarian aid, as agricultural and pastoral activities are severely disrupted by insecurity.Oxfam conducted a vulnerability analysis that reinforces the findings of other studies demonstrating the deterioration of communities’ resilience. Indeed, the Diffa region faces multiple crises—some predictable (the effects of climate change, such as droughts and floods) and others unpredictable (attacks by crop pests, population influxes, and forced displacement). The MSNA analysis conducted by Oxfam confirms that the food situation is cause for concern. In Bosso, approximately 85% of households have an acceptable food consumptionscore (FCS), while 15% are at borderline or low levels. In contrast, in Chetimari andKabalewa, nearly 30% of households already have borderline food consumption, and between 7% and 12% have low food consumption. The situation is particularly alarming in Toumour, where more than 92% of households have a borderline or low FCS: only 7.4% have an acceptable FCS, compared to 50% with borderline consumption and 43% with low consumption. In these three municipalities, the DGD HUM’s Crisis Modifier, currently being activated, will enable rapid responses to help forcibly displaced populations meet their basic food needs. However, the municipality of N’Guiguimi—which is under significant pressure due to the displacement of more than 23,829 people and has just been identified as a priority municipality for FRAHOC 2026 funding (following an initial presentation on June 25, 2026, to UN and NGO country management teams, ahead of the official publication), is the focus of this intervention.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education for all, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam Novibs main office is based in The Netherlands, it supports the work of a network of local offices, the implementation of global projects, fund raising, campaigning and advocacy. The Hub Niamey Niger exists since 2006 as a humanitarian field office and since 2012 as the decentralized Country office for Oxfam Novib, dealing with all the development and humanitarian themes like Sustainable livelihoods, Right to Basic services, Humanitarian and resilience interventions, The right to be heard and the right to an Identity, including women's rights and sexual and reproductive health rights. The Country Office in Niger works with local partners to realize the vision of a Niger without poverty
